title: ZX Spectrum tape
description: What goes on a tape and how it loads: the loading scheme, the blocks it loads and where, where it jumps once they have, and its loading screen. The tape designer opens it as a page; scripts/build_tape.py builds it.

meta.description: About the file rather than the tape. The builder ignores all of it.

comment.description: Prose for whoever opens the file.

scheme.description: How the tape loads. "zx-tape-loader": the fast loader in examples/zx-tape-loader, with a screen revealed in a designed order. "rom": the Spectrum's own LOAD "", a BASIC loader then each file at normal speed.

loaderAddress.description: zx-tape-loader only: where its 433-byte loader runs, anywhere in $8000-$FFFF. null is the top of RAM, $FE4E.

loadingScreen.description: The *.screen.json that is the tape's loading screen, relative to this file; null for none.

blocks.description: What the tape loads after its screen, in tape order, keyed by name.

file.description: The file the bytes come from, relative to this file.

offset.description: Where in the file the block starts. 0 if left out.

length.description: How many bytes. The rest of the file if left out.

entry.description: Where the program starts once everything has loaded.

stack.description: The address the BASIC loader CLEARs: RAMTOP, with the machine stack just below it, and the program entered on that stack. zx-tape-loader: from $5F41 (its own, just above the BASIC, when null) up to just below the loader; the loader's calls reach $1B below it. rom: at least just below the lowest block the BASIC allows; null for just below the lowest block; blocks keep $40 below it clear.

output.description: What to build, relative to this file: a .tap (rom only), a .tzx, a .wav or a .csw. Left out, the tape's own name as a .tap for rom and a .tzx for zx-tape-loader.
